title: Route temperature south of ex-USSR reserves did not clearly advance long-distance migrant bird arrival in 1950-2017; their local temperature response was less than half that of short-distance migrants
abstract: Question: does temperature on the migration route explain the spring arrival of long-distance migrant birds, and the post-1986 advance that local warming did not explain in the Chronicles of Nature Calendar (open item of sci:sha256:beea9c54)? Data: 18,707 first-arrival dates in 627 site x species series (>= 15 years) at 159 ex-USSR reserves, 1950-2017; migration classes from Storchova and Horak (2018): 126 long-distance and 501 short-distance series; NOAA GHCN-CAMS temperature; CRU TS Sahel rainfall. Method (plan written before the fits): local temperature L (60 days before mean arrival), route temperature U (box 8-20 degrees south, 75-15 days before mean arrival) and a north placebo box N; series means and linear trends removed; two-way (site, year) clustered intervals. Results: long-distance migrants arrived 0.70 days earlier per +1 C of local temperature (95% CI 0.42-0.99), short-distance migrants 1.56 (1.20-1.92); difference 0.86 (0.34-1.38). With L in the model, route temperature changed long-distance arrival by -0.19 days per C (-0.52 to +0.15), with the same sign in only 3 of 5 sector and period subsets, so the planned route hypothesis failed. The U-N contrast (-0.41) came from a positive N term in both classes (collinearity with L). Only a late route window (60-0 days before arrival) gave -0.48 (-0.95 to -0.01). In 1986-2017 the residual advance beyond local warming was -0.50 days per decade for long-distance and -0.85 for short-distance migrants; route temperature reduced the long-distance residual only to -0.43. Previous-year Sahel rainfall had no effect (+1.4 days per 100 mm, -0.8 to +3.6). Exploratory map: long-distance arrival followed temperature 20-30 degrees south of the sites (post hoc box -0.60, -0.94 to -0.26) and short-distance arrival followed boxes to the south-west (-0.52); these boxes were chosen with the same data. Limitations: first dates mix timing, population and effort; one box rule for all routes; long-distance data from 26 sites.

display.caption: Partial effects (days per +1 C, 95% two-way clustered CI) of local (L), route (U, 8-20 degrees south) and north placebo (N) temperature on first-arrival day of long-distance (blue) and short-distance (orange) migrants in ex-USSR reserves, 1950-2017. Upper block: pooled model and checks; lower block: planned sector and period subsets.

Exploratory: partial effect of temperature in 4 x 5 degree boxes displaced from each site (window 75-15 days before mean arrival), with local temperature in the model. Dots: |z| > 1.96 (no multiple-test correction). Solid box: planned route box; dashed box: planned north placebo box.

Observed 1986-2017 trends of first-arrival day and the parts predicted by local and by local + route temperature sensitivities, with site-bootstrap 95% CI. The residual advance is larger in short-distance migrants and route temperature does not remove it.

citations.reason: Same Chronicles of Nature data; we answer its open item on route temperature and migration-distance classes and confirm the lower temperature sensitivity of birds than of a fast-responding group, here long- vs short-distance migrants.
